prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: offshore/shore wind-farm O&M through Grid Interface Relay; excludes public grid/unrelated port operations. Objectives: safety/reliability/integrity/availability/environment. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System; Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy; Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway; Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver; Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone; Redoubt=Work Permit Portal. Turbine Controller produces Pitch Deviation Notice; local protection overrides authorized remote commands. SCADA Gateway flags work packages using notice; shall supply current status to permit reviewers on request. Control Engineer reviews alarms before commands; SCADA Engineer retains supervisory scope. Pitch System/Converter Cabinet/Nacelle Condition Monitor/Rotor Brake Unit/Turbine Sensor Bus support operation. Offshore Substation/Main Transformer collect/switch power; Export Cable Monitor monitors export. Work Permit Portal controls requests/revisions/reviews/authorization/execution/closure/audit. Requester identifies location/scope/duration/team/equipment. Duty Planner checks completeness, queues requests, resolves supply/scheduling before authorization; produces Transfer Manifest Addendum using Field Supervisor/Maintenance Planning Engine input. Reviews establish hazards/controls/access/coordination; HSE Officer reviews material risks; technical reviewers check compatibility; Marine Coordinator checks access; Vessel Master confirms transfers. Incomplete requests return with corrections. Authorizer permits only after recorded reviews/controls, bounded by scope/location/window/personnel. Field Supervisor validates prestart conditions; material changes require reassessment/may suspend authorization. Portal records start/pause/resumption/completion; responsible team reports completion/issues before closure. Maintenance Planning Engine uses reviewed conditions. Warehouse System produces Backorder Exception Slip for supply-date failures; Storekeeper/Spares Hub manage stock; Port Agent coordinates cargo/access. Personnel Tracking Console/North Access Scanner/South Access Scanner track personnel. Transport includes Daughter Craft/Service Operations Vessel/Helideck. AIS timestamps/Position Quality Flag; Marine Coordinator uses traffic/dispatch. Metocean Buoy logs offline; Weather Service validates/issues Squall Window Bulletin; Weather Analyst advises; Weather Hold requires safe-resumption confirmation. Blade Specialist reviews drone imagery; suspend unsafe flights; no physical-inspection substitution. Require authorization/logging/availability

New part:
S173: During normal operation, station service transformers at the Offshore Substation supply the facility's auxiliary electrical loads from the medium-voltage collection system.
S174: The normal supply serves control systems, lighting, ventilation, communications, and equipment required for safe switching and maintenance.
S175: Essential loads are separated from nonessential loads so that backup capacity can be reserved for safety and control functions.
S176: The Emergency Generator is assigned the operational alias Foxglove for maintenance and alarm references.
S177: On loss of the normal auxiliary supply, automatic controls initiate the Emergency Generator start sequence.
S178: Transfer to the emergency bus occurs only after voltage and frequency are within the configured acceptance limits.
S179: The transfer arrangement prevents the normal and emergency sources from being connected in parallel unless an approved synchronizing function is provided.
S180: The Emergency Generator supplies the designated emergency distribution bus and is not intended to support turbine export production.
S181: Loads connected to the emergency distribution bus are prioritized according to their contribution to personnel safety, equipment protection, and controlled shutdown.
S182: Nonessential loads are shed automatically when generator capacity is insufficient or the measured load exceeds its operating limit.
S183: If the Emergency Generator does not start or stabilize, the system raises an alarm and maintains any available uninterruptible control power.
S184: Operators use the approved recovery procedure to assess the fault, preserve essential services, and restore the normal supply when it is safe to do so.
S185: The Electrical Technician verifies protective device settings and transfer interlocks during planned maintenance.
S186: Scheduled exercising confirms that the Emergency Generator can start, accept its expected load, and operate for the required test duration.
S187: Fuel condition, cooling, lubrication, battery readiness, and exhaust ventilation are checked as part of the generator readiness program.
S188: Maintenance Planning Engine schedules inspections and corrective work using equipment condition and operating history.
S189: Morrowick maintains the designated emergency distribution bus within its approved operating limits.
S190: The Grid Interface Relay provides status indications that support assessment of the normal supply and its protective state.
S191: The Turbine Controller enters its configured safe operating mode when required auxiliary services are unavailable.
S192: The SCADA Gateway presents supply alarms and generator status to the Shore Control Room for remote awareness.
S193: The Control Engineer reviews persistent alarms and coordinates electrical support with the Substation Operator.
S194: Metocean Buoy produces the Wave Burst Record at the configured sampling interval.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
